content.title: Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid score, stats, highlights, result, talking points as Vinicius settles derby classic
content.text: JUMP TO:Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid scoreMatch statsHighlights, key momentsReaction from Alvaro Arbeloa and Diego SimeoneUpcoming games for both sidesReal Madrid battled to a thrilling win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday as Vinicius Junior scored twice in a 3-2 victory at the Santiago Bernabeu. Los Blancos knew they needed to respond to leaders Barcelona's 1-0 defeat of Rayo Vallecano earlier in the day, but things looked ominous after Ademola Lookman had put Atleti ahead at halftime after a brilliant assist from Giuliano Simeone.But Alvaro Arbeloa's team responded in the second period, Vinicius smashing home a penalty before in-form Federico Valverde pounced on a defensive mix-up to turn the game on its head.Nahuel Molina blasted home a quite incredible long-range goal to make it 2-2, but Vinicius cut infield and curled home the winner after some superb play from substitute Trent Alexander-Arnold.Valverde was then sent off in a contentious incident, referee Jose Luis Munuera Montero deeming him to have committed a deliberate act of serious foul play by kicking Alex Baena, although it looked as though the Madrid midfielder was trying to win the ball.Julian Alvarez rattled the post as Atleti pushed for an equaliser, but Madrid held firm for what could be three hugely important points.Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid score ScoreGoal scorersReal Madrid3Vinicius 52', 72', Valverde 55'Atletico Madrid2Lookman 33', Molina 66'Location: Santiago Bernabeu (Madrid, Spain)Referee: Jose Luis Munuera MonteroStarting lineups:Real Madrid (4-4-2, right to left): Lunin (GK) — Carvajal, Rudiger, Huijsen, F. Atleti are back level.Watch in USA | UK Valverde puts Madrid aheadFederico Valverde's spectacular form continues!Watch in USA | UK Vinicius levelsVinicius makes no mistake from the penalty spotWatch in USALookman strikes firstAdemola Lookman puts Atletico ahead against the run of play.Watch in USA | UK Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid talking points, analysisVinicius, Madrid dig deep to sustain title battleAfter Barca battled to three points against Rayo, anything but a Madrid win today would have felt fatal to their title chances.Heading into the international break, the Blaugrana hold a four-point lead with nine games left. The final Clasico of the league season has been scheduled for May 10, and if the gap remains the same, that match could prove decisive in this title race.With players now heading off for the international break, this felt like a pivotal victory for Arbeloa and his team. Had Barca extended the gap at the top, these two weeks would have weighed heavily on Madrid shoulders. As it is, they will feel confident that their rivals' lead is not insurmountable.Oh, and the Catalans' first game back in April? Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano.Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid reactionAlvaro Arbeloa"We showed character and mental strength. We had to suffer with one less player. I have a different view of the red card, but I thank [referee] Jose Luis for coming to explain to me why he sent him off. We were able to take the three points, which is what we wanted."[The referee] told me that it was excessive force, and I don't consider it as such. There is no intent to hurt or injure the opponent. It's my view, different from his. But he came to explain it, and I appreciate that. Sometimes it's appreciated, even if it doesn't change anything. The red card made everything more difficult and we had to suffer a lot. Every victory is a turning point. Now comes a fight for the league."On Vinicius: "He had another great game. It was another demonstration of talent, of courage, of not being afraid, of failing and trying again. As I always say, we're extremely lucky to have him."Diego Simeone"I don't think the result was because of the referee. We had the opportunity to take advantage of situations that arose during the match and we weren't able to take that step forward and win a game that, I believe, we at least deserved a bit more from."We had a match that, after the first goal, we could have controlled differently. We could have defended their goals better, we could have done more in attack, and that should serve as a lesson for what's to come. We have big opponents coming up and, with any minimal chance you give them, they will hurt you."On Lookman: "Lookman is growing, working very well. He's been giving us different things in attack, and we need that. We're helping him to improve defensively, so he can help us there as well, because he has that ability. He's a guy with a huge heart and an incredible willingness to learn and improve. That's fantastic, and hopefully he'll keep giving us important things like he did today."Real Madrid vs. Atletico Madrid upcoming schedulesReal Madrid upcoming fixturesDateCompetitionMatchSat, April 4La LigaMallorca vs. Real MadridTue, April 7Champions LeagueReal Madrid vs. Bayern MunichSat, April 10La LigaReal Madrid vs. GironaAtletico Madrid upcoming fixturesDateCompetitionMatchSat, April 4La LigaAtletico Madrid vs. BarcelonaWed, April 8Champions LeagueBarcelona vs. Atletico MadridSun, April 11La LigaSevilla vs. Atletico Madrid
